## Resources located

### 1. Fifth-grade English grammar warm-up
**[Challenging English Grammar Quiz for Grade 5 (ProProfs)](https://www.proprofs.com/quiz-school/quizzes/pp-challenging-english-grammar-quiz-for-grade-5)**

This appears suitable as a brief, online, multiple-choice warm-up: the page labels it **Grade 5th**, has **8 questions**, and starts with a straightforward conjunction question. It also includes sentence structure, verb forms, pronouns, and tenses. For a student who benefits from highly scannable text, use its **Start Quiz** view and present one item at a time.

**Small teacher-preview note:** a few items (such as passive voice and dangling modifiers) may be more challenging than a typical fifth-grade review. I would use the clearer items first—conjunctions, adjective form, verb form, and pronouns—or read the questions aloud as needed.

### 2. Introductory marketing / 4 Ps classroom activity
**[Episode 211: The Marketing Mix — classroom guide PDF (DCMP)](https://dcmp.org/guides/TID7070.pdf)**

This is a printable classroom guide for *The Marketing Mix*. The listing identifies it as **17 pages** and introduces the problem of how to let a target market know about a product or service. It appears appropriate for an eighth-grade introduction because it focuses on the marketing mix and the central ideas of **product, price, place, and promotion**. It should work well as a teacher-led activity: have students choose a familiar or invented product and complete a simple four-box plan—one box for each P.

### 3. One Slidesgo template for the combined lesson
**[Back to School Activities for Middle School (Slidesgo)](https://slidesgo.com/theme/back-to-school-activities-for-middle-school)**

This is a **free**, editable Google Slides/PowerPoint template. Slidesgo describes it as creative, colorful, illustrated, and game-based, and labels it for **Middle School**. That makes it a fun, age-appropriate choice for a combined grammar warm-up plus marketing activity. You can replace its existing prompts with: (1) the bionic-reading introduction, (2) grammar-quiz directions, (3) a four-Ps mini-lesson, and (4) the marketing-plan work slide.

I kept the three relevant resource pages open for reference.

## First-slide introduction in bionic-reading style

**To**day we will **warm** up with a **short** **gram**mar quiz, then **prac**tice how **peo**ple use **ba**sic **mar**keting **strat**egies like **prod**uct, **price**, **place**, and **pro**motion. **Read** each **dir**ection **care**fully and do your **best**.
